references.text: The background for the Spirit resting on Eldad and Medad; God promised to take some of the Spirit that was on Moses and put it on the seventy elders.
Describes how the Spirit came upon the elders who were gathered at the tent, and they prophesied.
Moses' response when Joshua wanted to stop Eldad and Medad: he wished that all the Lord's people were prophets and that the Lord would put his Spirit on them.
Joel's prophecy that God will pour out his Spirit on all people, and they shall prophesy—an expansion of what happened with Eldad and Medad.
Saul met a group of prophets, and the Spirit of the Lord came upon him so that he prophesied among them, similar to how the Spirit came upon Eldad and Medad.
God's Spirit came upon Saul's messengers and upon Saul himself, and they prophesied—showing that the Spirit can come unexpectedly upon people outside the usual gathering.
Pentecost when the Holy Spirit was poured out on all the believers, and they began to speak in tongues—the fulfillment of Moses' wish that all God's people should be prophets.
Paul's teaching about the gift of prophecy and that all can prophesy—linked to the theme of spiritual gifts given to believers outside a formal setting.
